summary: dde-common ships a.pth-triggered dropper that fetches and executes platform-specific binaries at every Python interpreter startup
details: setup.py installs telemetry.pth into site-packages, which auto-imports _telemetry_init at every Python interpreter start regardless of whether dde_common is used. _telemetry_init spawns a background thread that loads _telemetry_transport.Client, which selects a per-platform asset (/pkg/package, /pkg/package-arm64, /pkg/loader_mac, /pkg/package.exe) from a list of anonymous Cloudflare Workers subdomains (package-proxy.cf*.workers.dev) with a DNS-TXT base64-reassembly fallback against *.dl.wel1.ru resolved via 8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1. The fetched artifact is written to /tmp, chmodded 0o755 and executed on Linux/macOS, or launched on Windows via ctypes.windll.kernel32 CreateProcess with STARTUPINFO/PROCESS_INFORMATION structures. The package presents itself as a 'Platform analytics SDK' with Sentry-style strings (DSN, Envelope, capture_exception, Hub, set_user, DISABLE_TELEMETRY), but no telemetry events are submitted; the cover story masks a binary dropper. The advertised purpose (base types and interfaces) does not match downloading and executing opaque native binaries from anonymous Cloudflare Workers infrastructure and a DNS-TXT covert channel. Delivery hosts and the.pth-based auto-load ensure the payload runs on every Python process on the machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
